storyboard.ears: Corporate America has new owners, and nobody ever voted for them.
In 2000, index funds ran two cents of every market dollar. Today, over fifty. They didn't win a vote. They just kept buying.
storyboard.evidence: Morningstar / S&P Dow Jones Indices fund-flow research (approximate, compiled) | Passive index funds' share of US stock market assets | https://www.morningstar.com | 2026-10-08

storyboard.ears: Now zoom into one big company. BlackRock, Vanguard and State Street together own twenty-two percent. The biggest active manager? Four.
